analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The changed ranges are base line 578 and head lines 578 and 580-586, in the capacity performance-measurement table. The edit clarifies that sample_age_ms is measured from the newest observation, even when an older completed observation arrives later. It also notes that the Swift producer (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe) applies the same age rule per workload bucket and posture series. It states that completed samples keep the existing receipt-order EWMA and sample counts, and that wire fields are unchanged. The three supplied units are base text (lines 584-1451), so the changed lines 578-586 are not directly visible except through the patch excerpt. Even so, the patch is complete and contains only documentation text.

Security relevance: this touches transient capacity and freshness telemetry, which is routing and availability evidence rather than authorization, attestation, encryption or billing. The base text states this telemetry is diagnostic. It also says the coordinator uses count, epoch and age to prevent heartbeat replay from refreshing old samples. The doc change makes this age semantic stricter and does not weaken any described control.

I did not map it to a threat entry. No change alters T-053, T-054 or the T-041 cache posture (TTL, HMAC names, scope). It also adds no new wire fields, trust grants or exposure of prompt content.

Remaining unverified: the claimed Swift behavior in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift is outside the supplied evidence. If that code differs from the docs, it could affect staleness-based routing, which is an availability or quality concern rather than a confidentiality one. The platform-owned coordinator freshness logic (capacity_sample_freshness.go) was likewise not supplied. I found no concrete security regression from this documentation-only change.
